title: Bootstrap run manifest
description: machine-bootstrap-contract.md §5. The durable record of one machine-bootstrap run. It records CHOICES and HISTORY, never TRUTH (§7): every plan/status/resume/verify re-probes, and a recorded step is invalidated when the versions it was observed against change. Key order here IS the canonical serialization order.

schema.description: Pins FAMILY and MAJOR; the minor is deliberately free, because §4.1's forward-compat rule is the validator's to apply — a const on the full string would reject the newer-minor documents that rule exists to accept.

status.description: `open` is the only non-terminal status. A crashed run leaves an open run behind, which is why `abandon` exists (§10.2) — without it one interrupted run would block the machine permanently.

seeded_from.description: §5 — a profile id and HASH, never a filesystem path: a path can itself reveal operator layout.

plan_hash.description: §1.6 — sha256 over the canonical planned action set. The presented `runtime:settings --execute-plugin-management` carries it, and the executor refuses a plan whose hash diverged from the one the operator read (test #25).

boundary.description: §5 — MUST all be false; the artifact validator refuses the write otherwise.

auth.description: §5 — an ENUM, not a boolean, because probeMachineHostState genuinely distinguishes these. A boolean would collapse `unauthenticated` into `unknown` and let a `sandbox_limited` read masquerade as authenticated.

plugins.description: Test #31 — Claude never expects an `enabled`/`disabled` field, because Claude does not report one. Only Codex carries `disabled`.

codexHookStateProbe.description: 1.1 (S8a5) — the probe's PER-HANDLER Codex hook-state evidence. Plugin-level `state` above says nothing about a single explicitly disabled handler (`enabled = false` in `[hooks.state]`) whose sibling is enabled, which is exactly what let an attestation read current while a hook was off. STRUCTURALLY OPTIONAL — deliberately absent from codexHostProbe's `required` — so a 1.0 document still validates; SEMANTICALLY required for a current applicable attestation: the completion reducer stales an attestation whose probe carries no `observation: available` hook_state. `disabled_expected` lists every expected handler explicitly disabled; absence of an `enabled` key means ENABLED (verified on codex-cli 0.142.5), so only explicit `false` rows appear here. `observation` distinguishes a config that does not exist (`missing` — no hook was ever trusted) from one that could not be read (`unreadable` — state unknown); the reducer stales on both, the operator recovery differs.

status.description: §6 — `satisfied` is reserved for OBSERVED state. A step is never satisfied because the operator said so, because a previous run recorded it, or because a fragment was rendered. Only a post-probe promotes a step, and `unknown` is never satisfied.

blocked_by.description: §5/§6.1 — the predecessor edges. The registry is the authority for these (lib/step-registry.mjs); a copy carried in a manifest is operator-editable data and is never trusted for stage/applicability/declinable/edges.

fragment_applied.description: §5 — marks that THIS run rendered a fragment and a post-probe observed the operator applying it; distinct from a pre-existing matching config. The §8.1 `permission` proof is required IFF a permission.*.applied step carries true, so a machine whose permissions already matched does not trip a proof it never needed.

invalidated.description: §7 — stamped when a recorded step is reset to `pending` because the runtime version, either host CLI version, or any installed plugin version in the selection changed since probed_at. A step satisfied against Codex 0.136 says nothing about 0.140.

boundVersions.description: §8.1 — binds EVERY selected plugin version, per host, not only runtime + the two CLIs. Freshness compares exact key SETS and values; a missing or null required version never counts as current.

status.description: §5 — the AGGREGATE, recomputed from `directions` on every read and NEVER trusted from storage. A smoke that passed claude->codex and failed codex->claude is `failed` (test #22); a stored `passed` would be a claim the evidence contradicts.

directions.description: §8.1 — a per-direction RESULT MAP, not a list of direction names. A schema that could only say `directions: [...]` could not express a one-way failure at all. BOTH keys are required: an empty map would let a `passed` aggregate be stored with no evidence behind it at all, which is precisely the forgery the per-direction shape exists to prevent. A direction that did not run says so with `absent`.

hookAttestation.description: §5/§8.1 — carries its own Codex-bound versions and the EXACT retained Codex-hook-bearing plugin set, and stales on a Codex CLI change, a hook-plugin add/remove/version change, or a disabled expected hook (test #24) — enforced at the INDIVIDUAL-HANDLER grain via probe hosts.codex.hook_state (S8a5): a handler explicitly disabled beside an enabled sibling still stales the claim, and a probe with no available hook_state observation never supports a current one. Runtime cannot query Codex `/hooks` trust non-interactively, so this records an operator CLAIM, never host truth (ADR-0030).

completion.description: §8 — the reduced completion verdict reduceCompletion writes. Extracted to a $def so the reducer's output can be validated against exactly this shape (the seam that caught the reasons/directions mismatch before wiring).

missing_steps.description: §6.1 — a step ABSENT from steps[] is counted here and BLOCKS completion. Without this a manifest that simply omits a required step passes the reducer, which is the exact false-pass this command exists to prevent (test #11).

evaluatedProof.description: §8 — the REDUCED proof reduceCompletion writes into `completion.proofs`: a recomputed AGGREGATE status plus its reasons, NOT the recorded per-direction `proof` (that stays in the proof/ files and keeps its `directions`). The directions collapse into `status`; step_id/declined/required/reasons are the reduction's own fields. A distinct def because the reduced shape is not the recorded shape — reusing `proof` here is the mismatch that would reject every persisted completion once the reducer is wired.

bound_versions.description: The recorded proof's bound versions (or null when no proof was recorded). Inlined as nullable because the validator implements a closed subset with no anyOf — a $ref cannot also carry `type: null` here.

hookAttestationVerdict.description: §8 — the REDUCED hook attestation reduceCompletion writes into `completion.hook_attestation`: the recomputed currency `status` plus its reasons. The recorded operator claim is `hookAttestation`; this is the verdict computed over it, and it carries `reasons` the closed `hookAttestation` def rejects — hence a separate def.
